text.p: Typhoon Carlo continues to threaten shipping as it moves north-northeastward well east-southeast of Japan. Carlo will gradually weaken and become extratropical over the next 48 hours as the storm takes a more northeasterly track. Carlo will continue to threaten shipping in the northwestern Pacific during this time.

Hurricane Lili remains a threat to shipping. The center of the storm is 1240 miles west southwest of the Azores, moving east northeast at 15 mph. Top wind are 85 mph, and weakening is expected this period while the storm increases its foward speed to the east northeast while losing tropical characteristics. The remnants of Lili could bring heavy rains and high winds to northwestern Europe this weekend.

Tropical cyclone 05a has stalled in the Arabia Sea to the south of Gujarat and well west of Bombay. It is expected to move slowly towards the north-northwest during the next 24 hours and then turn towards the west. This should keep the center from reaching India's coast but it still does bear watching. This system is a significant risk to shipping through the northeast Arabian Sea.

A disturbance is still causing squalls in through the Andaman Islands of the southeast Bay of Bengal. It is somewhat of a risk to shipping in the area. The threat to shipping may increase if the storm develops further, which it may.
